Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

I am Professor Nagesh Ham, Faculty Member, Department of Science and Humanities.

Key details

  • This is the second session of MadLab.
  • In this session we shall discuss the concept of data types, relational operators and logical operators.
  • Data types are those which define the type of data that we are using.
  • Every data type stores data that is in a form of a matrix or array.
  • Some common data types are integers, floating point numbers, scalar, character, strings and arrays.
  • An integer is a whole number.
  • There is not a fraction that can be positive, negative or zero.
  • Note that when two integers are added, subtracted or multiplied, then the corresponding result is also an integer.
  • 2 multiplied by 8, etc When one integer is divided by another integer, the corresponding result may be an integer or a fraction.
  • Six by three, that is two.
  • Floating point numbers.
  • As a name indicates, floating point numbers are numbers that contain floating decimal points.
  • Zero point zero one etcetera are floating point numbers.
  • When a calculation includes a floating point number, it is called a floating point calculation.
  • Any number which is used to represent a quantity is called a scalar.
  • This includes integers, complex numbers, floating point numbers.
  • character single alpha numeric symbol enclosed in a single code is a character constant.
  • The first one is a numerical constant.
  • The one which is enclosed in a single code is a character constant.
  • Any two or more alpha numeric symbols enclosed in a single code is called a string.
  • Arrays List of similar data in a single row or a column is called an array.
  • Elements can be numerical or character or strings.
  • The four types of arrays are zeros function, i function, once function and ran function.
  • Zero's function.
  • As the name indicates, it creates a matrix of all zeros.
  • It creates an identity matrix.
  • One's function.
  • It creates a matrix of all ones.
  • It generates random numbers between 0 and 1 that are distributed uniformly.
